notes: C+ model (D51): one uniform character scale, head+hair as a single scaled group, separate weapon correction.
Every factor carries an evidence status. VERIFIED_ALPHA means the value comes from Cube.exe code/data; PROXY_NOT_ALPHA means a documented technical approximation.

The head/torso width ratio is NOT rescaled by the engine: part sizes come from the authored .cub voxel counts (VoxelModel +0x44/+0x48/+0x4c are voxel counts) and Creature_drawModel centres parts by -0.5*size in voxel units. creature_getScaleVec4 returns (1,1,1,1) for a normal creature, so no per-part scale exists for body/head/hair.

Weapon scale: Creature_drawModel applies mat4_scaleAxes to the item model in the hand for specific weapon types (0.5 / 0.6 / 0.8 found). The greatsword class is mapped to 0.6 (PARTIAL: the weapon-type byte +0xaa9 to item-class mapping is not fully proven).

Attachment offsets found in set_vec3_offset_by_id (node ids 0x1a/0x1e -> z -0.9, 0x21 -> -0.2, 0x4a -> -0.3, 0x4b -> +0.1, 0x97 -> -0.35) are in voxel units; they are recorded for future rig work and are not applied to the proxy assembly.

Hair tint: the character colour triple (+0x1a0..0x1a2 of the creation widget) is written into the appearance struct (+0x10..+0x12) and consumed by creature_generateAppearance, i.e. the original game bakes the colour into the generated appearance instead of a runtime shader. The exact replacement code path is not recoverable from the inspected pseudo-C, so the pilot implements the approved T3 mask tint and marks it PARTIAL.

body.evidence: creature_getScaleVec4 returns (1,1,1,1) for a normal creature; no per-part scale in Creature_drawModel for body parts

head_hair.evidence: head and hair share the 18x16x16 authoring grid; the engine scales the whole creature uniformly, so the group stays 1.0 relative to the body
head_hair.singleApplication: applied on the head node only; hair is its child and inherits the scale exactly once

weapon.evidence: Creature_drawModel: mat4_scaleAxes(0x3f19999a=0.6) around the in-hand weapon draw for weapon type 0x0c; 0.5 and 0.8 exist for other types

artisticVariants.note: Optional looks for the producer's visual decision. NOT applied by default, never reported as Alpha values.

head_small.purpose: smaller head for a less stylised silhouette

notes: T3: the original palette is preserved vertex-by-vertex; only vertices whose source voxel colour is listed in maskColors are blended with the tint colour in the shader.
maskColors = pure red (the hair's paint marker) and pure white (the hair's light base tone); both belong to the authored hair palette, every other colour stays untouched.
Pure RGB markers are never deleted automatically; hide lists stay explicit in assembly.json.
Decorative red voxels that are not in the mask stay untouched (verified per voxel coordinate).
